target_customer: Oncologists, health systems and pharma using RNA based diagnostics to predict immunotherapy response
problem: Single analyte biomarkers such as PD-L1 predict immunotherapy response poorly, so many cancer patients get treatments that do not work.
business_model: Clinical diagnostics (lab developed test billed to payers, with Medicare coverage) plus research and pharma services

founders.name: Jarret Glasscock
founders.background_notes: YC page names him as leader; one directory calls him co-founder and CTO. A CEO transition was announced in January 2025 per Business Wire.

founders.name: Dave Messina
founders.background_notes: Listed under former founders on the YC page with 25+ years in healthcare.

technical_complexity.rationale: Building validated RNA-seq biomarkers and machine learning models predicting immunotherapy response needed lab, bioinformatics and clinical validation expertise.

defensibility.rationale: Clinical validation (CAP and AMP peer review, trials) and Medicare coverage create barriers; proprietary clinical datasets compound.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition reported. Labcorp made a strategic investment in December 2025 rather than buying the company.

market_need_then: Immuno-oncology was expanding quickly with hundreds of companies and over 2,000 drugs in development by 2018 (2018 press release), creating demand for response predictors.

branding.brand_signature: Tagline 'The Leaders in RNA' and the OncoPrism assay name

brand_strength.rationale: Science brand known in diagnostics circles; no sourced press about the brand itself.

pivots.from: RNA sequencing services and research platform
pivots.why: Series A press focused on bringing RNA to precision medicine; the pivot date is approximate and not stated by a source.

outcome_analysis: Cofactor raised an 18 million dollar Series A in 2017 led by Menlo Ventures, built the OncoPrism immunotherapy response test, obtained Medicare coverage in 2024 and ran the PREDAPT trial. A December 2025 strategic investment from Labcorp and Ascension Ventures supports commercial expansion. It remains independent and small, with long diagnostic timelines and reimbursement as the main constraints.
notes: Wikipedia gives a 2008 founding and lists the company as a sequencing service born at Washington University; the YC page says 2015. No dated 2015 competitor source was found (CB Insights lists NanoString and Foundation Medicine but is undated), so competitors are empty. SEC Form D filings exist (CIK 1710475) but were not opened. CB Insights lists a 1.17M Series B-II in August 2023 and total raised 21 to 27.7M, unverified. Seed amount unknown; seed date from aggregators. Messina's Pioneer Fund role is from 2019, after founding.
